page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX and AVX-512 instructions. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression also registers in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all achieving average ratings. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks consistently perform in the average tier, though the PassMark memory score is weak.

Given the high memory density relative to the 12 dedicated vCPUs, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. The average performance in multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and Redis SET operations makes it suitable for in-memory caching, database hosting, and moderate multi-threaded processing. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks, high-throughput static web serving, or intensive LLM inference on larger models.
